instructions.question: What feeling does this Czech Facebook comment express: positive (thanks, wishes, praise, delight, craving the product), negative (complaint, frustration, sadness, insult, sarcastic attack), or neutral (factual, asking, requesting, joking or chatty with no clear feeling)?
instructions.rule: Positive needs feeling as the main message: standalone thanks, wishes, craving the product, or praise of the product, ad or animals, even mild. Thanks closing a question or explanation, contest requests, agreement with users, slogan-like promo statements, joy about non-brand things and smiley-decorated facts are neutral. Negative needs frustration, a complaint, objection to a brand decision, regret over a removed product, an insult, crying emoticons, or sarcasm against the brand. Irony, musing or teasing, price facts, plain 'why' questions and flat fault reports are neutral; if the feeling is weak or only implied, choose neutral.

neutral.what: Questions, requests, contest entries, information, promo-style statements, price facts, plain fault reports, user banter, irony or teasing, jokes, hopes, and factual notes with mild regret.
examples: jak deaktivuji službu Útrata?? (how do I deactivate the Útrata service??)
slevomat dává možnost zažít stále nové a nové zážitky (Slevomat lets you have ever new experiences)
takže si to bohužel kontrolovat nemůžeme... (so unfortunately we can't check it...)
a co třeba kdybys to vyřešil sám? :D konkurence ... ? (and how about solving it yourself? :D the competition ... ?)
neutral.cues: jak (how), prosím (please), předem díky (thanks in advance), snad (hopefully), bohužel (unfortunately), :D in banter
neutral.not_for: Fed-up complaints, crying ':(((' outbursts, objections to brand decisions and name-calling are negative.

positive.what: Standalone thanks, congratulations, good wishes, praise of products, ads, animals or photos (even mild), delight, loyalty, and craving the product.
examples: Díky za odpověď :-) (Thanks for the answer)
Držím pěsti!!! (Fingers crossed!!!)
mě chutnalo ;) (I liked the taste)
Dal bych si :P (I'd have some)
positive.cues: děkuji, díky (thank you), všechno nejlepší (all the best), chutnalo (tasted good), super, krásné (beautiful), dal bych si (I'd have some)
positive.not_for: Thanks closing a question ('...? Děkuji za info.' (Thanks for the info.)), 'mě by se hodily tři' (I could use three), and 'Už mám objednáno =)' (I've already ordered) are neutral.

negative.what: Complaints about price, service or product, objections to brand decisions, regret over removed products, threats to leave, sarcasm or mockery of the brand, insults, and frustrated outbursts.
examples: Jdu si do trafiky pro simku konkurence, už mě to přestává bavit. (I'm going to get a competitor's SIM, I'm getting fed up.)
bez prasátka to už neni ono :D (without the piggy it's not the same)
zase jsem to nestih, poslední dobou mi skoro pokaždý tyhle bomba akce utečou přímo před očima :-( (I missed it again; lately these great deals nearly always slip away right in front of me)
negative.cues: předražený (overpriced), už nikdy (never again), nechápu (I don't get it), už neni ono (it's not the same anymore), stále nefunguje (still not working), chudák (poor thing), :(((
negative.not_for: Factual problem reports, mild 'bohužel', price facts, and polite irony at other users are neutral.
